albums.album: At the Pershing: But Not for Me
albums.blurb: Recorded live on January 16, 1958 at the Pershing Hotel's lounge in Chicago, with Israel Crosby on bass and Vernel Fournier on drums. Jamal's spacious, dynamically restrained trio style was a direct influence on Miles Davis, and this set — anchored by the crossover hit "Poinciana" — is the recording that made him a national name.
albums.reception: The album spent 107 weeks on the Billboard album chart, reached number three, and has sold more than a million copies.

albums.blurb: Miller's sixth studio album, released posthumously in January 2020, was conceived as a companion to 2018's Swimming — the two titles completing the phrase "swimming in circles." Producer Jon Brion, who began the sessions with Miller, finished the record after his death in September 2018; the result is more sung than rapped, closer to soft-focus pop-soul than the hip-hop of his early catalog.
albums.reception: Circles debuted at number three on the Billboard 200 with 164,000 first-week units — Miller's biggest opening week — and holds a Metacritic score of 83.

albums.blurb: Cleo Sol is a West London singer best known as the lead voice of the anonymous collective SAULT and a recurring guest on Little Simz records. Rose in the Dark is her debut full-length, produced entirely by Inflo — the producer behind SAULT and Little Simz's Sometimes I Might Be Introvert — and blends intimate gospel-rooted R&B with touches of dub, bossa nova, and acoustic blues.
albums.reception: AllMusic rated the album 4.5 stars and selected it among its favorite albums of 2020, and it appeared on year-end lists from Clash and Complex.
